title: Unsung Heroes of the Court
summary: Josh and Chuck introduce new writer Olivia Greshawn and cover three unsung courtroom roles: bailiffs, court stenographers (court reporters), and court sketch artists. The bailiff segment traces the job from medieval English manor overseers and French baillis to the modern American court security officer, covers duties (handling evidence, swearing in witnesses, guarding juries, evictions), pay, and celebrity bailiffs Petrie Hawkins Bird (Judge Judy) and Rusty Barrell (People's Court, Divorce Court). The court reporting segment covers clay-tablet legal records in Mesopotamia, early American record-keeping and the nineteenth-century push for official court reporters, Greg shorthand and Tironian notes, Miles Bartholomew's stenotype machine, steno masks, real-time transcription and speech-to-text, pay, and a court reporter whose drinking problem led to missed trial records. The sketch artist segment covers the origins of courtroom sketches in the 1859 John Brown trial, the ban on cameras in courtrooms after the Hauptmann trial, sketch artists such as Howard Brody, Bill Robles, Jane Rosenberg and Arthur Lien, the Supreme Court no-camera rule, and the Tom Brady deflategate sketch. The episode ends with a listener mail from Kayla about dentistry history (G.V. Black and Saint Apollonia).
topics: Judge Judy bailiff Petrie Hawkins Bird

segments.title: Opening and new writer announcement
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck promote a live show in San Francisco and introduce new writer Olivia Greshawn, previewing the three-part episode on courtroom bailiffs, stenographers, and sketch artists.

segments.title: Bailiffs: history and duties
segments.summary: The bailiff's history runs from English manor overseers and French baillis to the modern American court security officer. Duties include handling evidence, swearing in witnesses, guarding juries, and keeping order. Pay is discussed, along with the fact that bailiffs in some states also do evictions.

segments.title: Celebrity bailiffs
segments.summary: Petrie Hawkins Bird was Judge Judy's bailiff for twenty-five seasons, and was not invited to join her new show. Rusty Barrell was a real Los Angeles County bailiff who became a TV bailiff on Divorce Court and The People's Court and worked with Judge Joseph Wapner.

segments.title: Court reporting: origins and early records
segments.summary: Court records go back to Neo-Babylonian clay tablets. In the US, judges were not required to write down verdicts until the early nineteenth century, and Massachusetts and Congress passed laws on official reporters. Before that, freelance reporters sold transcripts.

segments.title: Shorthand history and the stenotype
segments.summary: Shorthand is traced from Tiro's Latin shorthand through medieval monks to the Gregg method. Miles Bartholomew's stenotype machine changed the field. The machine has about twenty-two keys and lets a writer type whole words at once, and experienced reporters can reach around 300 words per minute.

segments.title: Steno masks, real-time transcription, and reporter pressures
segments.summary: The steno mask is described as a silenced way to re-voice proceedings for later transcription. Real-time transcripts are now sent to judges and lawyers, and speech-to-text tools are discussed along with their limits on accents and overlapping speech. Pay and training time are mentioned. A reporter's drinking problem caused missed trial records and reconstruction hearings.

segments.title: Courtroom sketch artists
segments.summary: Sketch artists emerged when cameras were barred from courtrooms after the 1859 John Brown trial and the Hauptmann trial. Notable artists include Howard Brody, Bill Robles, Jane Rosenberg, and Arthur Lien. The Supreme Court still bars cameras, and the Tom Brady deflategate sketch became a meme. Attorneys sometimes frame their sketches.

segments.title: Listener mail: dentistry history
segments.summary: Kayla writes to add details to the earlier dentistry episode, noting G. V. Black's pedal-driven drill and cavity preparation method, and Saint Apollonia, patron saint of dentistry.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck thank Kayla and close the episode with the show's production credit and where to find more podcasts.
